description_full: Everforth, Inc. provides information technology solutions for commercial and government sectors in the United States, Canada, and Europe. It operates through two segments: Commercial and Federal Government. The Commercial Segment provides consulting, creative digital marketing, and permanent placement services primarily to Fortune 1000 and mid-market companies across harmonized solutions areas, such as cloud and infrastructure, data and AI, software development and engineering, customer experience, cybersecurity, and enterprise platforms, as well as key industries consists financial services, consumer and industrial, technology, media and telecom, healthcare, and business and government services. The Federal Government Segment provides advanced IT solutions in data and AI, cybersecurity, and enterprise platforms to defense and intelligence, national security, federal civilian, and other clients in the public and private sectors. It provides its products under the Apex Systems, Creative Circle, CyberCoders, ECS, GlideFast, and TopBloc brand names. It holds a strategic partnership with WisdomAI, Inc. to turn enterprise data into AI-powered decisions. The company was formerly known as ASGN Incorporated and changed its name to Everforth, Inc. in April 2026. The company was founded in 1985 and is headquartered in Glen Allen, Virginia.

financial_summary: Everforth, Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $1.5B market cap on $4.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -5% over the past three years and +7% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 30%.

The business throws off $288M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.89× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.9× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 3.4×.

Management returns a meaningful 11.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 3.4% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
